sample_unit: patients (All of Us development cohort; BioMe external validation N=9,818)
models_evaluated: M5 social determinants of health model

links.outcome: Discrimination of models applied without retraining in external BioMe cohort versus All of Us development
links.effect: Discrimination was attenuated in BioMe (M4 AUROC 0.659) compared with All of Us (M1 0.673 to M5 0.797); predicted probabilities shifted systematically upward.
links.quote: In Bio  Me , discrimination was attenuated (M4 AUROC 0.659), but the relative ordering of information layers was fully preserved, and a systematic upward shift in predicted probability distributions underscored the need for recalibration before deployment in a new setting.

links.outcome: Calibration of predicted probabilities when models applied to a new setting without retraining
links.effect: A systematic upward shift in predicted probability distributions in BioMe indicated the need for recalibration before deployment in a new setting.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating nested models under a fixed screening policy (constant 90% specificity) to isolate the effect of added data layers
Adding laboratory, medication, longitudinal trajectory, and SDOH features to improve risk observability and recover missed cases

screen.reason: The study empirically tests a deployment practice framework (a fixed-policy threshold targeting 90% specificity across layered data sources including SDOH and longitudinal trajectory) to evaluate risk observability and missed-case recovery in external validation cohorts.

primary.practice: fixed-specificity screening policy evaluation across data layers
